citation.title: Multi-material Multi-physics Topology Optimization with Physics-informed Gaussian Process Priors
citation.authors: Xiangyu Sun; Shirin Hosseinmardi; Amin Yousefpour; Ramin Bostanabad
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (publisher full text requires purchase)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the 2D MBB beam under a mass constraint, the learned method has median compliance 1.049 versus 0.982 for ordered SIMP and 0.987 for PolyMat, with similar reported constraint values.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No quantitative speed comparison with a classical method is given for this outcome.
claim.alternatives: §4.1 Table 4 reports other compliance comparisons; §4.4 Table 15 reports higher actuator and gripper displacement than COMSOL; §5 qualitatively says PIGP has higher training cost than SIMP and COMSOL is slower.

baseline.classical_method: Ordered SIMP and PolyMat (§4.1); SIMP 3D (§4.1); COMSOL MMA (§4.4)
baseline.implementation: Open-source ordered SIMP, PolyMat, and SIMP 3D codes; commercial COMSOL (§4)
baseline.problem_size: MBB 2D: ordered SIMP 301 × 151 FE nodes; PolyMat 45413 nodes; PIGP 201 × 101 to 401 × 201 collocation points (§4.1, Table 3)
baseline.classical_iterations: COMSOL: three continuation stages of 500 iterations each (§4.4); SIMP/PolyMat stopping rule not stated
baseline.training_time: Up to 10,000 epochs for benchmark PIGP (§4.1); 20,000 for thermomechanical PIGP (§4.4); wall time not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; per-problem learning uses no offline data set (§3–4)
baseline.quality_metric: FE-evaluated compliance and mass/cost constraints (§4.1, Table 4)
baseline.quality_gap: MBB 2D mass case: median compliance PIGP 1.049, ordered SIMP 0.982, PolyMat 0.987 (§4.1, Table 4)

R1.evidence: §4.1 Table 4: primary comparison concerns compliance, with no speed outcome.

R2.evidence: §4.1 Table 4: primary comparison concerns compliance, with no speed outcome.

R3.evidence: §3–4: model parameters are optimized for each design problem, with no offline training set.

R4.evidence: §4 and Table 4: final designs are FE evaluated and mass/cost values reported, but a rate of failed or infeasible designs is not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 4 compliance geometries in 2D and 3D (§4.1), 2 heat cases (§4.2), 2 mechanism cases (§4.3), 2 thermomechanical cases (§4.4), each with multiple material/constraint settings

notes: §4 says ten random initializations per experiment. §5 describes higher training costs than SIMP without numeric runtimes. Declarations state code is available via GitHub upon publication, and the preprint links its repository; runnable benchmark and licence cannot be established from the coded text.
